strategies.name: break_and_retest_continuation
strategies.entry_summary: Identify an obvious key level such as pre-market high/low, previous day high/low, or the 30-minute opening range high/low. Enter only after price breaks the level with strong momentum and volume, then retests it and shows confirmation that the level is holding in the breakout direction: bullish cand
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop on the opposite side of the breakout level, often just beyond the confirmation candle / break area. Target the next obvious area of liquidity such as a previous high/low or supply/demand zone; the speaker also mentions trimming and moving the remainder to breakeven in some examples.

variants.timeframe_note: Examples shown on 5-minute and 2-minute charts; also references Asia session and New York session contexts
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: After a strong break above resistance, wait for the retest to hold as support and use bullish price action such as long
variants.target_note: Next obvious liquidity above, such as previous high or pre-market high; sometimes trim partials and move rest to breake
variants.transcript_quote: Price breaks above a key level, it comes back, it retests that level, and it holds it, and it continues in the original direction.

variants.timeframe_note: Examples shown on 5-minute and 2-minute charts; also references Asia session and New York session contexts
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: After a strong break below support, wait for the retest to hold as resistance and use bearish price action such as long
variants.target_note: Next obvious liquidity below, such as previous low or another demand/liquidity area; sometimes trim partials and move r
variants.transcript_quote: Price ends up breaking below the support, well now we have the break, we're waiting for price to come back up and retest it as resistance. If it can

consensus.enumeration_note: The video teaches one break-and-retest continuation skeleton; long and short executions are opposite-direction variants of the same setup with mirrored entry, stop, and liquidity-target rules, not separately taught management frameworks.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: step number one is you want to identify your key level. Again, pre-market highs, pre-market lows, the 30-minute opening range high and low, uhprevious
entry_sequence.rationale: Again, pre-market highs, pre-market lows, the 30-minute opening range high and low, uh previous day's highs, previous day's lows, a strong area of support or resistance.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: Step number two is we want to wait for price to break the key level.
entry_sequence.action: wait for price to break the key level
entry_sequence.rationale: So, we want strong momentum either at the breakout above resistance or the break below the support level.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: step number three, we want to wait for the retest
entry_sequence.rationale: We want to wait for price to pull back

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: step number four is going to be the entry. I enter after confirmation.
entry_sequence.rationale: we want to see bullish price action. Long lower wicks, bullish hammers, dragonfly dojis, etc. That would help confirm to us that this resistance is now becoming support. Or if we're looking at this scenario right here, when price breaks below, when it comes back up, we're looking for bearish price action. Long upper wicks, uh bearish hammers, gravestone dojis, etc.

stop.rationale: Your stop is if price breaks back on the opposite side of the breakout level. That's it.

strategies.stop_management: Maybe caught a trim, maybe two trims, and stopped the rest break even, but still offered opportunity.
